question: The digital transformation of Greece’s Electronic National Social Security Entity (e-EFKA), which was financed with significant resources from the Recovery and Resilience Facility, includes, among other things, the digitisation of insurance history and the development of a new integrated information system.

The relevant milestone (134a) stipulates the delivery of the projects – confirmed with an acceptance report from the relevant monitoring committee – as a criterion for completion, with completion scheduled by the end of 20251. Regulation (EU) 2021/241 links disbursements to the satisfactory fulfilment of agreed milestones and targets2.

However, key subsystems of the new integrated information system became operational in summer 20263,4, raising a legitimate question: is the formal delivery of an IT project sufficient to assess its successful implementation, or is it also necessary to examine its actual operational functioning and effectiveness? With this in mind, can the Commission say: 1.
Beyond the delivery report, what substantive and qualitative criteria will it use to assess the full implementation of milestone 134a?
Will it check whether the new system was actually put into operation and provided the intended services by the milestone’s scheduled completion date?
Does it assess, prior to disbursement, measurable outcomes such as a reduction in processing times, backlogs and service issues affecting insured persons?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (13.11.

2026) The digital transformation of Greece’s Single Pension Fund’s (e-EFKA) is part of a broader measure in Greece’s Recovery and Resilience Plan (RRP) which is financed by the Recovery and Resilience Facility (RRF)1 and aims to upgrade and expand the digital infrastructures of public authorities in charge of labour market monitoring and social security issues in Greece.

According to Regulation (EU) 2021/241, the RRF is a performance-based financing instrument. Member States submit payment requests to the Commission and the Commission releases funds to Member States only after it has assessed the satisfactory fulfilment of the agreed milestones and targets that are set out in the respective Council Implementing Decision (CID)2 and the Annex that is attached to it3.

The related milestone requires the delivery of the following projects as confirmed by the acceptance protocol of the related project monitoring committee: (1) Integrated Information System for labour market monitoring – Work card; (2) Unified flow of employment and insurance data – Overhaul of the Integrated Information System for labour inspection (ARIADNE); (3) Digitisation of the insurance history of the Single Pension Fund (e-EFKA) and support of the pension awarding system; (4) Development of a New integrated Information System for e-EFKA; and (5) Occupational Health and Safety System (HERIDANOS).

The completion of the above milestone was expected for the fourth quarter of 2025 indeed, but this was an indicative timeline. The Greek authorities provided evidence for this particular milestone as part of the last payment request that was submitted on 29 September 2026, and whose assessment is still ongoing4.
1 The Recovery and Resilience Facility was set up in 2021 to provide loans and grants to EU Member States to

support national reforms and investments with a view to mitigating the economic and social impact of the coronavirus pandemic and making European economies and societies more sustainable, resilient and better prepared for the challenges and opportunities of the green and digital transitions. For the related legislation, see https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/PDF/?uri=CELEX:32021R0241.

4 More information about Greece’s RRP and the assessment of the payment requests to date: https://reformsinvestments.ec.europa.eu/recovery-and-resilience-facility-1/country-pages/greeces-recovery-and-resilienceplan_en?prefLang=es#further-information.
